status: Implemented; default and Worker validation passed
change: Ordinary unlimited row ordering now detaches retained rows under the query allocation scope, admits each directory append before mutation, and admits native stable-sort workspace. Bounded selection consumers no longer redundantly sort the already ordered winners.

validation.additionalBoundaryRun: Seven query-row-top-k-memory tests passed after adding exact measured peak and one-byte-short unlimited ordering cases
cases: scanner closure and sibling ownership preservation
validation.remoteEvidence: Explicit borrowed-row adapter over real Parquet HTTP 206 and ignored-range 200 responses, four concurrent full-order queries, repeated after cache reuse. Final cache eviction releases all pool usage. Worker suite passed, but this explicit fallback fixture is HTTP-only.

limitations: Sort workspace charges are explicit conservative units, not a portable measurement of native sort or VM heap.
Stateful sort runs, checkpoint serialization/deserialization, hive merge and result projection/output admission remain separate gaps.
Per-row directory reservation overhead requires measurement; no latency improvement is claimed.
